rv.q: They are enough for each other, and reason enough to see this “Jenufa.”
The evening, inevitably, was about music and singing—and there, they got things just right.

That the highly touted production proved the most negligible part of the experience in no way detracted from the evening, which was musically and expressively as affecting as one will find at the Met this season, Jenůfa is great because it does what opera is designed to do, as well as it can be done.
The biggest issue with this production is that it looked empty and unfinished on the massive Met stage.

cn.t: Critics rave over the Met's *Jenůfa*, with Asmik Grigorian's soaring soprano earning particular acclaim. Claus Guth's production wisely steps aside to let Janáček's raw, incandescent opera and its fearless cast shine.
